packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-01 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure / method statement
- No proposed identification or earlier reading of this text was in my context. This is a blind reading.
- Beyond viewing the 15 images: I made enlarged, contrast-stretched greyscale crops of some tiles (PIL, written to a separate scratch folder, not the packet folder) to help read faint offsets. No other files, web or search tools were used.
- All 15 images loaded.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only)
- image-001 (reduced overview) and image-008 (reduced overview) show the two inner faces of a book binding: wooden boards with leather turn-ins, five sewing supports laced through the board near the spine. Both photographs appear horizontally mirrored: the typed paper label on image-001 ("De Koninklijke Vlaamsche Academie heeft dit boek verworven door aankoop van de E.H. Peeters, te Hechtel, in het jaar 1929.") reads in mirror image. In the mirrored photos the manuscript text reads left-to-right normally, which suggests the text on the boards is an offset (ink transfer from a former pastedown) or reversed residue; I cannot tell which from the images. A round paper shelf-label "...10" is at top left of image-001.
- The text on the boards is faint brown offset in a small gothic textualis/glossing hand with heavy abbreviation, frequent "ff." and "C." sigla and "l." / "ar." markers, i.e. dense prose with legal-style allegations (observation of sigla; interpretation as legal commentary is tentative). Small red touches (paraph marks / initials) appear at line starts in several places (image-002, image-004, image-005, image-009, image-010, image-012, image-015).
- image-001 board: one column of text visible along the left side (spine side in the photo), largely obscured by the typed label in the middle; residue of a second column to the right of the label near its lower edge (image-001, below label, centre-right) and a small block lower right (around the lower sewing support). Top-left area is mostly lost.
- image-008 board: two narrow surviving strips of text: a column in the centre (tiles image-012, image-013, image-014, image-015) and a column at right next to the spine (tiles image-009, image-010, image-011). The left half of the board is blank/abraded.
- Sewing-support strips (parchment, visible through the board slots) carry a few letters: image-003 slot "...ene ?dar..." / "...?na..."; image-009 slot "...ulare ?ret..." / "...?oc?ti..."; image-008 top slot "...elit..." / "...pt ?pro...". Too little to use.
- No running titles, no visible column of lemma vs. commentary distinction (no underlined lemmata seen). Column order between the two board faces is unknown.

SPANS SELECTED
A. image-009 lower half + image-010 + image-011: right-hand column of the image-008 board (best continuous block, ~35 lines).
B. image-014 + image-015 (with image-013 overlap): centre column of the image-008 board.
C. image-004 lower part + image-005 + image-006: column of the image-001 board below the label.
Overlaps: image-009 last lines = image-010 first lines; image-010 last lines = image-011 first lines; image-013 bottom = image-014 top; image-014 bottom = image-015 top; image-004 bottom = image-005 top; image-005 bottom = image-006 top; image-002 bottom = image-003 top. Repeated lines are noted, not counted twice.
Unread / largely unread: image-002 (narrow right-aligned line-ends only), image-007 (faint residue right of label), image-012 upper part, image-001 upper left, and the right halves of most lines in span C where the text fades into the abraded area.

Line numbers are counted from the top of each image; partial lines at the top edge count as line 1. Readings are of faint offset text; most words are uncertain.

LIMITATIONS
- This is faint offset/residue text on wooden boards, photographed in mirror image; most individual words are uncertain and many readings above are guesses marked with "?". Treat only the phrases flagged as "most secure" as usable for matching.
- Large parts of the image-001 board are covered by the 1929 typed label; the image-008 board is abraded on its left half.
- Column order and which face precedes which cannot be determined from these images.
- Sigla "ff." and "C." are visually clear in many places; numbers after them (e.g. "xx.", "vii.") are uncertain.
- Wider view needed: a non-mirrored, raking-light or UV image of both boards, and a view under/around the typed label, would substantially improve the reading.
